title: pm-dispatch: inside a Claude Code project, dispatch each card as its own thread, and choose the dispatch effort by the card's difficulty
body:
**Maintainer request.** Filed by `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549), `os-bill`, session `session_01B2EeooonSXrANpkpgUSfFZ`, on the maintainer's word in this session's project chat. ⛔ Not a claim. Lane and grade are triage's. The surface is `.claude/**`, a governed surface at **Tier S** (AGENTS.md rule 14): it lands once a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS record stands on the PR's head and every check is green, through the owning seat. ⚠️ Corrected: this line first said "by human merge", which was wrong.

**The maintainer's words, verbatim:**
- 「你能识别到在项目的环境下工作吗？此时就每张卡开新线程。」
- 「立一张卡，修改 skills，包括派任务时要求根据任务的难度来选择 effort」
- 「并发加到2 ，你现在就可以开一个新的thread」 (spec seat 2's batch).
- 「还是需要你来总体调度，因为要优先派 p1」 (to the project's coordinator).
- 「同意」, to the coordinator's proposal: S-class mechanical cards are done by an in-seat subagent; M and up, `priority:p1` and `security` cards get their own thread.
- 「更新 skills issue」 (this update).

## Why

This seat has run inside a Claude Code project thread for its whole current shift. Each card's dev ran as an in-seat subagent, all of them on the thread's one designated push branch. Measured frictions:
- The maintainer cannot see a dev's work until it hands back. #25092's dev ran for more than two hours with nothing visible.
- Every card serialises on the one branch, reset from `main` after each merge.
- The dispatch effort is never chosen: the harness sets a subagent's or thread's effort only when the maintainer's words or a skill ask for it, and `pm-dispatch` does not.

A project gives each thread its own branch, checklist and PR watch, and the project's coordinator opens threads on a seat's request and can set a thread's model and effort at creation.

## What the skill should say

1. **Recognise the project environment.** A seat whose session is a project thread (the project-thread tools, such as the coordinator channel, are loaded) dispatches each card as its own thread, a new dispatch backend beside `mode:subagent` and `mode:cloud`. The seat asks the coordinator to open the card's thread with the dispatch order. The seat keeps the claim, the order, the contract review, the `## 席位核对` ACCEPT, landing and the landing record. The card thread implements, opens the draft PR and drives its CI.
   - A card under the disclosure ruling (#9387, `5323310017`), whose private detail must not leave the seat's own session, stays an in-seat subagent. The claim says so.
   - A card thread counts against `batch` as a subagent does.
   - The claim's `Branch:` and session identity name the card thread's branch and session, not the seat's. How the claim records an identity the seat learns only after the thread opens is for the PR to settle.
   - **Which cards get a thread (maintainer's 「同意」):** S-class mechanical cards (a prose fix, a label, a regenerated artifact) stay in-seat as a subagent, because a thread re-clones the repository and re-reads the skill and `os-dev.md` before it starts. M and up, `priority:p1` and `security` cards get their own thread.
   - **Who schedules (maintainer's 「还是需要你来总体调度，因为要优先派 p1」):** the project's coordinator schedules card threads across every seat, `p1` first. A seat sends the coordinator its candidate cards at any time, each with its priority, dispatch-order file and suggested effort, without waiting for its own slot. The coordinator opens the threads in priority order under a project-wide cap, the sum of the seats' `batch` terms. The seat tells the coordinator when a card thread finishes or its PR merges, so the slot is freed.
   - **Order and claim mechanics measured on the first two card threads (#25168, #25185):** the order lives in the project's shared folder (`/mnt/project-files/<seat>/dispatch-<N>.md`), because a thread cannot read the seat's scratchpad. The card thread posts the claim itself from the seat's text, filling in its own session and designated branch, because `check-closing-target-claim.mjs` needs the claim's `Branch:` to be the PR's head branch, which the seat learns only after the thread opens. The coordinator sets a thread's model and effort only on the maintainer's explicit word, so the seat attaches the maintainer's message when it asks. The thread hands back to the seat thread in one message and stays open for review FAIL items.
2. **Choose the dispatch effort by the card's difficulty**, as a field of its own beside the model tier, in the claim's `Container & model:` line and in the dispatch order (the subagent's effort, or the effort the coordinator opens the thread with). A starting proposal for the PR to settle:
   - `medium`: S, mechanical (prose, regenerated artifacts, one-line refusals with a precedent).
   - `high`: M, the default.
   - `xhigh`: L/XL; `security` or `priority:p1` cards; the contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; decision analysis on the four axes.
   - `max`: only when the maintainer names it.
   The skill's own rule is what lets a seat set it: without that rule, the harness leaves effort unset.

## Expected surfaces

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` (the args table's `mode:` row, the claim template's `Container & model:` line), `references/dispatch-runbook.md` (the backends), `references/execution-duties.md` (collecting from a card thread), and `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` where it assumes a subagent. One changeset or `skip-changeset`, as the governed-surface rules say.
